interest: This file is intriguing because it documents how memorials and commemorative acts intersected with diplomacy and international relations even amid escalating tensions prior to and during World War II. The record of the First Lord of the British Admiralty sending a commemorative message for the dedication of the Togo Shrine in Tokyo in late May 1940 highlights lingering naval respect for Japan's Russo-Japanese War hero Admiral Togo, even on the eve of the Pacific War and during the Battle of France. Additionally, the inquiries regarding a memorial monument in Yokohama to an American Consul General reflect historical memory, consular heritage, and transatlantic/transpacific ecclesiastical connections involving Trinity Church in New York.
overview: This file consists of U.S. Department of State 'List of Papers' docket sheets under decimal classification 894.413, which pertains to monuments, statues, and memorials erected in Japan. Page 1 indexes a May 28, 1940 telegram from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew in Tokyo concerning the dedication of a shrine to Admiral Marquis Heihachiro Togo and noting a message sent for the occasion by the First Lord of the British Admiralty (cross-referenced to file 894.44 Togo, Marquis/26). Page 2 indexes May 1944 (or 1914) correspondence with G. Gebhardt regarding the erection of a monument in Yokohama to the memory of American Consul General J. R. S. Morris, including references to Trinity Church in New York City.

subfiles.summary: Department of State List of Papers docket sheet (Form DS-46) for decimal file 894.413, recording Serial No. 25. It indexes Telegram No. 389 sent at 10 p.m. on May 28, 1940, by Ambassador Joseph C. Grew from Japan regarding the dedication of a shrine to the memory of Admiral Marquis Togo. The entry quotes the text of a message from the First Lord of the British Admiralty on the occasion and cross-references the primary document filed under 894.44 Togo, Marquis/26.

subfiles.about: A State Department List of Papers sheet recording correspondence concerning a monument in Yokohama commemorating American Consul General J. R. S. Morris.
subfiles.summary: Department of State List of Papers sheet (Form 592, Page 4) under decimal file 894.413 indexing Sub No. 26. It records an incoming inquiry from G. Gebhardt concerning the erection of a monument in Yokohama dedicated to American Consul General J. R. S. Morris, noting connections with Trinity Church in New York City. A subsequent entry dated May 24 records the State Department's reply providing information regarding the inquiry.
